title: Make, do and take: uses and phrases
subtitle: make a mistake, do your best, take a break
summary: Learn which nouns go with make, do and take, and the common phrases built from these three verbs.

lesson.heading: Things we make, do and take
lesson.note: These word partners (collocations) are often different in other languages, so learn them carefully.

lesson.heading: When two verbs are possible
lesson.text: With a few nouns, more than one verb works. Both forms are correct and mean the same.

examples.text: I'm **doing** / **taking** a Spanish course next month.
I'm just going to **take** / **have** a shower.
**Take** / **Have** a look at these pictures.
We must **make** / **take** a decision.
I don't **do** / **take** much exercise.

lesson.heading: make = cause or force
lesson.text: **Make** can mean to cause something to happen, or to cause a particular state. It can also mean to force someone to do something. Note the form: make someone **do** (no *to*).

examples.text: I like Boris - he **makes** me laugh.
It **made** them angry when Karen refused to help.
My parents **made** me do my homework when I was a child.
The police **made** us wait outside the main gates.
When he shouted out the wrong answer, it **made** him look stupid.

lesson.heading: make friends, make up your mind
lesson.text: If you **make friends with** someone, you get to know them and like them. If you **make up your mind**, you decide something.

examples.text: I **made friends with** a couple of guys from Canada when I was on holiday.
He's **made up his mind** to leave work at the end of next month.
They still haven't **made up their minds** about the holiday.

lesson.heading: do
lesson.text: We use **do** for a general action when we don't know what the action is, or when there is no noun. If you **do your hair** or **do your make-up**, you make it look nice. If you **do your best**, you try as hard as possible.

examples.text: What shall we **do** this afternoon?
Don't just stand there, **do** something.
I'll just **do** my hair, then we can go out.
I'm not a good student, but I always **do my best**.
I've **done** nothing today.

lesson.heading: Meanings of take
rows: I took the key out of my pocket.
Did he take the job they offered him? Do they take credit cards?
I took notes during the meeting.

lesson.heading: take it easy, take a break
lesson.text: If you **take it easy** or **take things easy**, you relax and don't do very much. If you **take a break**, you stop work and rest for a short time.

examples.text: I'll **take things easy** today.
Let's **take** a ten-minute **break**.
I'm tired of writing this report. I'm going to **take a break**.

lesson.text: When you meet a new noun, write down the verb that goes with it: *make an effort*, *do the housework*, *take a photo*.

exercises.prompt: Which verb goes with each noun?
Did he ___ many mistakes in the test?
It was too difficult. I couldn't ___ the homework.
exercises.explanation: We do our homework and do the housework.

exercises.statement: They did a lot of noise at the party.
exercises.explanation: They made a lot of noise at the party. We make a noise.

exercises.prompt: How many photos did they ___ at the wedding?
We didn't want to leave, but they ___ go.
exercises.explanation: Make someone do something = force them. Note: made us go, not made us to go.

exercises.prompt: I'm not very good at this, but I'm ___.
exercises.explanation: Do your best = try as hard as possible.

exercises.prompt: OK, let's stop work and ___ for ten minutes.
exercises.explanation: Take a break = stop work and rest for a short time.

exercises.prompt: He isn't lazy at all. He is definitely ___.
I've ___ up my mind. I'm going to go to Thailand for my holiday.
We ___ friends with Andrés when we were in the same class last year.
exercises.explanation: Make friends with someone = get to know them and like them.

exercises.prompt: I'm going to relax and do nothing this weekend. I'm going to ___.
exercises.explanation: Take it easy / take things easy = relax and don't do much.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.right: get to know them and like them
